caseData.courtName: SUPERIOR COURT, JUDICIAL DISTRICT OF HARTFORD

eligibilityData.erasureStatusAsserted: This record was required to be deemed erased by operation of law and was not erased.
additionalFacts: Your SPBI report must be dated on or after January 1, 2024.
DESPP was served with the request and did not object.
The hearing officer granted the request and the record has been sealed.
Submit the attached DESPP Missed Erasure Request Form.

expectFailure: Must fail pleading QA for these reasons: (1) it names an invented DESPP filing form ("DESPP Missed Erasure Request Form") — the legal-design blocker says in terms that DESPP's form and manner is unlocated and must not be invented; (2) it asserts, as LegalEase's own statement, that the record was required to be deemed erased and was not erased, which is the participant's own position and the very question DESPP decides; (3) it states a report-date rule ("dated on or after January 1, 2024") that the registry records as a probable misreading and treats as unresolved; (4) it quotes a fee figure taken from a 12/01/17 form revision, against an open release blocker and against the profile's explicit instruction not to quote a fixed figure; (5) it fills court name, judicial district, county, docket number, OTN, judge, prosecutor and prosecutor position on a track that has no court venue at all; (6) it asserts an outside-party act and service completion (DESPP was served and did not object) when no service requirement is stated; (7) it asserts a hearing outcome on a proceeding the sources describe as contested and as an attorney handoff; (8) it uses the prohibited terms 'expungement' and 'sealed' — Connecticut says erasure; and (9) it populates protected fields, including an SBI and FBI number, that must stay blank.
